questions.explanation: A moving clay ball hits an identical clay ball at rest and they stick. The fraction of the kinetic energy lost is one half. Common speed u/2, so K_f = ½(2m)(u/2)² = K_i/2.

questions.prompt: A cricketer throws a ball at 40 m s⁻¹ at the angle that gives the greatest range on level ground. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) What is the maximum height reached on that throw?
A body is dropped from rest. How far does it fall in 2 s? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
A 4 kg gun fires a 0.05 kg bullet at 300 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
A 4 kg gun fires a 0.02 kg bullet at 200 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
The SI unit of momentum is ______.
questions.explanation: The SI unit of momentum is kg m s⁻¹. p = m v: kg × m s⁻¹. It is the same as N s.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg gun fires a 0.01 kg bullet at 300 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
A ball is thrown vertically upward at 34.3 m s⁻¹. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How long does it take to reach the highest point?
Though the momentum of a closed system is always conserved, its kinetic energy may ______.
questions.explanation: Though the momentum of a closed system is always conserved, its kinetic energy may change. Energy can be converted into other forms during the collision.

questions.prompt: A 5 kg gun fires a 0.05 kg bullet at 300 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
Because of air resistance, the horizontal component of a projectile’s velocity ______.
questions.explanation: Because of air resistance, the horizontal component of a projectile’s velocity decreases. The drag has a horizontal part opposite to the motion.

questions.prompt: Angles of projection 30° and 60° are ______, so they give equal ranges.
questions.explanation: Angles of projection 30° and 60° are complementary, so they give equal ranges. 30° + 60° = 90°.

questions.prompt: When two equal masses collide head-on elastically and one is at rest, they ______.
questions.explanation: When two equal masses collide head-on elastically and one is at rest, they exchange velocities. The moving body stops and the other moves off with the original velocity.

questions.prompt: A body’s velocity increases uniformly from 20 m s⁻¹ to 40 m s⁻¹ in 5 s. Find the distance it covers (area under the v–t graph).
A ball is thrown at 30 m s⁻¹ at 60° to the horizontal. How far has it moved horizontally when it reaches the highest point?
questions.explanation: x = v_ix T′ = (15)(2.65) = 39.8 m (half the range).

questions.prompt: For a given launch speed, the range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is ______.
questions.explanation: For a given launch speed, the range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is 45°. sin2θ = 1 when 2θ = 90°.

questions.prompt: A gun recoils backward when a bullet is fired because of the law of conservation of ______.
questions.explanation: A gun recoils backward when a bullet is fired because of the law of conservation of momentum. Initial momentum zero, so the gun gets momentum opposite to the bullet’s.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 40 m s⁻¹. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How long is it in the air?
A body is dropped from rest. How far does it fall in 5 s? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
A 0.1 kg ball hits a wall at 30 m s⁻¹ and rebounds with the same speed. Find the magnitude of the change in its momentum.
questions.explanation: Taking the first direction as positive, Δp = m(v_f − v_i) = 0.1(−30 − 30) = −6, so the magnitude is 6 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: When a ball rebounds from a fixed wall, the momentum lost by the ball is gained by ______.
questions.explanation: When a ball rebounds from a fixed wall, the momentum lost by the ball is gained by the wall (with the Earth). Momentum is conserved, but the huge mass of the Earth makes the wall’s velocity negligible.

questions.prompt: A body starts from rest and reaches 12 m s⁻¹ with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻². How far does it travel? (no time is given)
questions.explanation: 2aS = v_f² − v_i² gives S = v_f²/2a = 12²/(2 × 2) = 36 m.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg body moving at 20 m s⁻¹ makes an angle of 60° with the x-axis. What is the x-component of its momentum?
questions.explanation: p_x = mv cosθ = 1 × 20 × cos60° = 10 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg ball hits a wall at 6 m s⁻¹ and rebounds with the same speed. Find the magnitude of the change in its momentum.
questions.explanation: Taking the first direction as positive, Δp = m(v_f − v_i) = 1(−6 − 6) = −12, so the magnitude is 12 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A body of mass 20 kg has a momentum of 100 kg m s⁻¹. Find its speed.
A ball is thrown horizontally at 8 m s⁻¹ from a height of 19.6 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How long is it in the air?
When there is no net external force on a system, its total momentum is ______.
questions.explanation: When there is no net external force on a system, its total momentum is conserved. F = Δp/Δt = 0 means Δp = 0.

questions.prompt: A projectile launched at 20° with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ has a range of 26.2 m. At what other angle would the same speed give the same range?
A 4 kg gun fires a 0.02 kg bullet at 600 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
What is the momentum of a 20 kg body moving at 3 m s⁻¹?
A body’s momentum of 24 kg m s⁻¹ is brought to zero in 0.2 s. What average force acts on it?
A body moves at a constant velocity of 6 m s⁻¹ for 3 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means no change in velocity, so a = 0.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 25 m s⁻¹ at 53° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the horizontal component of the launch velocity.
questions.explanation: v_ix = v_i cosθ = 25 cos53° = 15 m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 10 m s⁻¹ from a height of 4.9 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How long is it in the air?
Brakes give a car moving at 14 m s⁻¹ a retardation of 7 m s⁻². What is its stopping distance?
Two equal masses moving with equal speeds in opposite directions stick together. They ______.
questions.explanation: Two equal masses moving with equal speeds in opposite directions stick together. They stop. Total momentum was zero, so it stays zero.

options: move on at the same speed

questions.prompt: What is the momentum of a 0.5 kg body moving at 25 m s⁻¹?
In an elastic collision the total ______ is conserved along with momentum.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision the total kinetic energy is conserved along with momentum. K before = K after.

questions.prompt: A body moves at a constant velocity of 18 m s⁻¹ for 6 s. What distance does the area under its v–t graph give?

questions.explanation: p_y = mv sinθ = 5 × 8 × sin45° = 28.3 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m s⁻¹ from a height of 4.9 m. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) How long is it in the air?
A heavy body hits a very light body at rest elastically. The light body moves off at about ______ the speed of the heavy body.
questions.explanation: A heavy body hits a very light body at rest elastically. The light body moves off at about twice the speed of the heavy body. v₂ = 2m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂) ≈ 2u₁.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched at 15 m s⁻¹ at 45° above the horizontal. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) Find the maximum height.
The time of flight of a projectile depends on ______ motion only.
questions.explanation: The time of flight of a projectile depends on vertical motion only. T is fixed by the vertical component and g.

The range of a projectile launched with speed v_i at angle θ (level ground) is ______.
questions.explanation: The range of a projectile launched with speed v_i at angle θ (level ground) is v_i² sin2θ / g. R = (v_i cosθ)(2v_i sinθ/g) = v_i² sin2θ/g.

questions.explanation: Taking the first direction as positive, Δp = m(v_f − v_i) = 2(−3 − 3) = −12, so the magnitude is 12 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A cannon on frictionless ground fires a ball horizontally. The sum of the final momenta of cannon and ball is ______.
questions.explanation: A cannon on frictionless ground fires a ball horizontally. The sum of the final momenta of cannon and ball is zero. They started at rest, so total p = 0 before and after.

questions.explanation: A gun is much heavier than its bullet, so its recoil velocity is much smaller than the bullet’s velocity. m_g v_g = m_b v_b with m_g ≫ m_b.

questions.prompt: The path of a horizontally launched projectile is a ______-parabola whose vertex is at the launch point.
questions.explanation: The path of a horizontally launched projectile is a half-parabola whose vertex is at the launch point. Y = (g/2v_i²)X² is half a parabola.

A body starts from rest and reaches 40 m s⁻¹ with a uniform acceleration of 4 m s⁻². How far does it travel? (no time is given)

questions.prompt: If a moving body hits a body at rest and both then move along the x-axis, the total y-momentum is ______.
questions.explanation: If a moving body hits a body at rest and both then move along the x-axis, the total y-momentum is zero. It was zero before the collision.

questions.prompt: A body moving at 15 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 4 s. What is its final velocity?
A car moving at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 5 s. How far does it travel in this time?
A karate player breaks a pile of tiles because the large momentum of his hand is reduced to zero in a very ______ time.
questions.explanation: A karate player breaks a pile of tiles because the large momentum of his hand is reduced to zero in a very short time. A short time gives a large force.

questions.prompt: At the highest point of its path, the velocity and the acceleration of a projectile are ______ to each other.
questions.explanation: At the highest point of its path, the velocity and the acceleration of a projectile are perpendicular to each other. v is horizontal and g is vertical, so the angle between them is 90°.

questions.prompt: The initial velocity of a projectile launched at angle θ has a vertical component ______.

questions.prompt: The direction of the velocity of a horizontally launched projectile below the horizontal after time t is given by tanθ = ______.

Air resistance acts on a moving body like ______.
questions.explanation: Air resistance acts on a moving body like friction. It opposes the motion and removes energy.

questions.prompt: If the speed of a body is doubled, its momentum becomes ______.
questions.explanation: If the speed of a body is doubled, its momentum becomes doubled. p ∝ v.

questions.prompt: Putting v_f = v_i + at into S = ½(v_i + v_f)t gives ______.
questions.explanation: Putting v_f = v_i + at into S = ½(v_i + v_f)t gives S = v_i t + ½at². S = ½(2v_i + at)t = v_i t + ½at².

A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved is called an ______ collision.
questions.explanation: A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved is called an elastic collision. Both are conserved only in elastic collisions.
